children: Major jewellery stocks were trading lower on Tuesday morning following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal to Indians to refrain from buying gold unless absolutely necessary.
Titan Company was trading at Rs 5,050 on the NSE at 9:53 am, down Rs 52.50, or 1.03%, from the previous close. Kalyan Jewellers India was trading at Rs 587.45, down Rs 13.55, or 2.25%.

Thangamayil Jewellery was trading at Rs 5,333.50, down Rs 78.50, or 1.45%, while BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle was at Rs 807.40, down Rs 10, or 1.22%. Senco Gold was the only major jewellery stock trading in the green, at Rs 353.35, up Rs 4.75, or 1.36%.

PM Modi made the appeal in a post on Instagram, urging Indians to embrace the mantra of "Swadeshi" and "Vocal for Local". He said people should avoid travelling abroad merely for leisure or hosting weddings in foreign countries, instead calling for "Weddings in India".

We should avoid traveling abroad merely for leisure or hosting weddings in foreign lands; instead, we should live by… https://t.co/5ad5RKJiG5 pic.twitter.com/PVN04APP3e
"We should also refrain from buying gold unless absolutely necessary," Modi said.
He added that greater emphasis on "Swadeshi" and self-reliance would help the country move towards becoming a "Viksit Bharat" by the time India marks 100 years of independence.
The appeal comes as gold remains a key purchase for Indian households, particularly for jewellery and weddings.

title: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, Thangamayil fall up to 2.25% as PM Modi again urges restraint on gold buying
